ai_assistance: Drafted with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code) from the team's cited agronomy package, FAO-56 and K-State sources; the team should check values against those sources. Disclosed per Space Apps AI rules.
notes: Values are regional starting points for western Kansas, not field-calibrated parameters.
A null means 'not evaluated': no sourced value was found tonight. Each null has a matching 'verify' note.
GDD values are °C·days with the 10/30 °C method (equivalent to the 50/86 °F method), counted from planting. K-State °F values were divided by 1.8.
Corn, sorghum and winter wheat are all grasses (family 'grass'): changing between them gives no automatic family-break credit (agronomy rule T1_R10_NO_FAMILY_OR_N_CREDIT).

crops.name: Corn (grain)

value_sources.season.plant_window: T1_NW_CORN_CALENDAR (regional sowing reference, as in agronomy.json corn_corn)
value_sources.season.harvest_window: T1_NASS_CALENDAR statewide historical most-active range, not a local deadline
value_sources.season.harvest: Middle of the T1_NASS_CALENDAR harvest range
value_sources.gdd_to_silking_c: KSU_CORN_GDD_LATEPLANT: ~1,500 °F GDU to silking for a 110-day hybrid → 833 °C·d, rounded to 835
value_sources.gdd_to_maturity_c: KSU_CORN_GDD_LATEPLANT: ~2,670 °F GDU to black layer for a 110-day hybrid → 1,483 °C·d, rounded to 1,485
value_sources.sensitive_window: Silking ± 100 °C·d (≈ ±1 week in July). Rule of thumb for the pollination period; evidence level C
value_sources.heat_threshold_c: 35 °C hot-day screen used across the dashboard (PLAN.md §3); a screening threshold, not a damage threshold
value_sources.kc: FAO-56 Table 12 maize (grain): ini 0.3, mid 1.20, end 0.60 (0.35 if field-dried)
value_sources.kc.stage_days: FAO-56 Table 11 maize (grain), April-planted row (Spain/California): 30/40/50/30 = 150 d. No Great Plains row exists
value_sources.root_depth_m: FAO-56 Table 22 maize 1.0–1.7 m; 1.5 m chosen for deep loess silt loams
value_sources.frost_free_days_needed: Derived: days from Apr 25 planting to 1,485 °C·d in NASA POWER 2021–2025 at the demo cell were 121–125; 125 used

verify: gdd_to_silking_c and gdd_to_maturity_c depend on hybrid relative maturity; the farmer's hybrid rating should replace them
kc.stage_days come from a non-Great-Plains FAO-56 row; total 150 d vs the 163-d Apr 25–Oct 5 calendar (the last ~2 weeks are field dry-down)
frost_free_days_needed is derived from only 5 years of POWER data at ~50 km resolution
sensitive_window width (±100 °C·d) is a rule of thumb

crops.name: Grain sorghum

value_sources.season.plant_window: T1_NASS_CALENDAR statewide historical range (as in agronomy.json corn_sorghum); local upper planting limit unresolved
value_sources.kc: FAO-56 Table 12 sorghum (grain): ini 0.3, mid 1.00–1.10 (1.05 used), end 0.55
value_sources.kc.stage_days: FAO-56 Table 11 sorghum (grain), May/June row listing USA: 20/35/40/30 = 125 d
value_sources.root_depth_m: FAO-56 Table 22 sorghum 1.0–2.0 m; 1.5 m chosen
value_sources.heat_threshold_c: Same 35 °C dashboard screen as corn; not a sorghum-specific damage threshold

verify: gdd_to_silking_c (half-bloom) is null: K-State gives ~1,500 °F GDD half-bloom → maturity on a 42 °F base (KSU_SORGHUM_GDD), but no planting → half-bloom value on the 10/30 °C method was sourced tonight
gdd_to_maturity_c is null for the same reason; the sensitive window is therefore not evaluated for sorghum
frost_free_days_needed is null: depends on hybrid maturity and planting date; K-State notes stress-delayed maturity raises frost exposure (T1_SORGHUM_GUIDE)
heat_threshold_c 35 is a common screen, not a sorghum pollen-viability threshold

crops.name: Winter wheat

value_sources.season.plant: T1_NW_WHEAT_CALENDAR: northwest Kansas target around September 25
value_sources.season.plant_window: T1_NASS_CALENDAR statewide historical range; do not treat Oct 20 as a northwest cutoff
value_sources.season.harvest_window: T1_NASS_CALENDAR statewide historical range; harvest is in the calendar year after sowing (harvest_year_offset 1)
value_sources.sensitive_window: Calendar-based (May 1 – Jun 15) because winter wheat GDD from autumn sowing is not comparable to the summer-crop method; K-State heat guidance is for flowering/grain fill
value_sources.heat_threshold_c: KSU_WHEAT_HEAT: damage worsens with prolonged temperatures above ~82 °F and yield is reduced with many hours above ~91 °F; 32 °C (~90 °F) daily max used as a screen
value_sources.kc: FAO-56 Table 12 winter wheat with frozen soils: ini 0.4, mid 1.15, end 0.25–0.4 (0.3 used)
value_sources.kc.stage_days: FAO-56 Table 11 winter wheat, October-planted Idaho USA row 160/75/75/25 = 335 d, scaled proportionally to the 278-d Sep 25 – Jun 30 calendar
value_sources.root_depth_m: FAO-56 Table 22 winter wheat 1.5–1.8 m; 1.5 m used

verify: gdd fields are null: winter wheat development (vernalization, dormancy) is not modelled with summer-crop GDD; use the calendar sensitive window
kc.stage_days are a proportional scaling of the Idaho row, not a published Great Plains row
heat_threshold_c 32 °C is a screening value between K-State's ~82 °F and ~91 °F statements
Establishment water after corn harvest is not modelled (agronomy rule T1_R05_WHEAT_HANDOFF)

crops.name: Fallow (no crop)

value_sources.kc: Rough bare-soil evaporation coefficient (FAO-56 Ch. 6: Kc ini for bare/sparse soil depends on wetting interval and soil; ~0.3 for infrequent wetting). Flat over 365 d

verify: Kc 0.3 is a ROUGH value: real bare-soil evaporation is high right after rain and near zero when the surface is dry; residue lowers it further
Fallow under residue is not the same as bare soil; NDVI cannot tell them apart

extra_sources.name: Late planting of corn: how location and hybrid maturity affect probability of success (K-State Agronomy eUpdate)
extra_sources.provider: Kansas State University Research and Extension
extra_sources.notes: States a 110-day hybrid needs ~1,500 GDU to silking and ~2,670 GDU to black layer (°F, 50/86 method). Retrieved 2026-11-15 via search summary; page text should be re-checked.

extra_sources.name: Sorghum Growth and Development, MF3234; and K-State eUpdate growing degree update for grain sorghum
extra_sources.provider: Kansas State University Research and Extension
extra_sources.notes: Most hybrids need ~1,900 GDU (35 °F base) or ~1,500 GDU (42 °F base) from half-bloom to physiological maturity. Also https://eupdate.agronomy.ksu.edu/article/growing-degree-update-for-grain-sorghum-417-5. Retrieved 2026-11-15.

extra_sources.name: Effects of High Temperatures on Wheat (K-State Agronomy eUpdate, Lollato and Redmond)
extra_sources.provider: Kansas State University Research and Extension
extra_sources.notes: Grain fill can recover from short heat; damage worsens with prolonged temperatures above ~82 °F; yield reductions associated with many hours above ~91 °F. Retrieved 2026-11-15.
